name: Pratte's Reef (permit name: Chevron Reef), El Segundo / Dockweiler Beach, California
status: DERIVED: every number in "global", "lines" and "extra_layers" is computed by the script from the published 3D-model data (no new measurement); the model inputs and their sources are in "key_inputs" and in the model METHODS_3D.md.

version.name: B  Phase I as installed (Sept 2000): outermost point approximately 6 ft below MLLW (Borrero & Nelsen 2003 p.2); top follows the seabed

frame: x alongshore (toward 155 deg T, SSE); y offshore (toward 245 deg T, WSW); origin on the MSL waterline (alongshore-uniform profile)
datum: z = metres above MSL (NOAA 9410840 Santa Monica, epoch 1983-2001); MSL - MLLW = 0.849 m; z_MSL = z_NAVD88 - 0.792 (DEM); LAT = -1.469 m MSL; MLLW = -0.849 m MSL
shoreline_definition: y = 0 is the MSL waterline: the z = 0 contour of the NOAA DEM mean cross-shore profile (model.js seabed.shoreline_y_m = 0, definition: "MSL waterline (z = 0 contour of the seabed profile)").
units: metres; offshore_m = model y (distance from the model shoreline y = 0, positive offshore); elevations in metres above MSL (z up); x = alongshore model axis

method.reef_surface: Re-implementation of build_3d.py reef_height_field(): h(x,y) = max(0, min(h_top, d_in/slope_run)), d_in = distance inside the toe outline (76-vertex Skelly Engineering design layout of 110 bags, no as-built plan exists), slope_run = 1.0 (ASSUMPTION A5), h_top = constant thickness z_ref - z_seabed(y_ref) = 1.349 m (state B: outermost point approx. 6 ft = 1.829 m below MLLW = -2.678 m MSL at the apex, Borrero and Nelsen 2003 p.2; assumption A4: top follows the seabed at constant thickness), >= one 1.2 m bag course; z = z_seabed(y) + h; 0.25 m grid.
method.seabed: model.js seabed.profile_z_m (5 m spacing, NOAA NGDC 2010 Santa Monica 1/3 arc-second NAVD88 DEM, mean of 31 alongshore stations +-150 m, z_MSL = z_NAVD88 - 0.792); alongshore-UNIFORM (no x dependence). Position of the reef on the profile is nominal (100 yd = 91.44 m from the waterline; +-25 m uncertainty, reef_offset_range_m).

sampling.interpolation: seabed: bilinear on the model grid / analytic profile; reef surface: NaN-aware (normalised) bilinear on the reef grid; profiles at constant model x
sampling.footprint_rule: a reef cell belongs to the footprint if (reef surface - natural seabed) >= 0.10 m (ASSUMPTION, avoids zero-thickness tapers)
sampling.crest_line: x of the shallowest reef-surface cell
sampling.crest_zone: contiguous points on the line within 0.10 m of the line maximum (ASSUMPTION)
sampling.ramp: seaward ramp = from the seaward edge of the crest zone to the seaward end of the reef run (the toe); ramp_length = horizontal distance, ramp_rise = reef-surface drop over it, mean_seaward_slope = rise/length
sampling.max_seaward_slope: maximum over the ramp of (z[y-1 m] - z[y+1 m]) / 2 m (central difference, 2 m baseline), tan, degrees and 1:n
sampling.toe: seaward toe = most offshore point of the reef run (reef surface still >= 0.10 m above the seabed); the reef elevation, seabed elevation and thickness there are reported (thickness > 0.5 m means the model surface is cut at its outline, not at the seabed)
sampling.gap_bridging: gaps up to 12 m along a line are bridged when forming the reef run (ASSUMPTION; only Narrowneck is affected)
sampling.alongshore_length: span = x_max - x_min of footprint cells with reef surface >= level; union = number of x-columns containing such a cell * dx. Two levels are reported because "crest -0.5 m" is ambiguous: (a) z >= -0.5 m MSL and (b) z >= crest - 0.5 m
sampling.offshore_distance: offshore_m is measured from the model shoreline y = 0 (definition in shoreline_definition); offshore_from_msl_line_m uses the first downward crossing of z = 0 (MSL) of the modelled natural seabed on the same line

key_inputs.input: plan outline (Skelly Engineering design drawing, 110 bags)

Outline traced and verified in `shape.json` (this project, verified 2026-10-04); the same drawing is Fig. 4 of S10

key_inputs.input: as-installed crest depth (-6 ft MLLW), bag size, dates

key_inputs.input: seabed: NOAA NGDC Santa Monica 1/3 arc-second NAVD88 DEM

sources.S5: NOAA National Geophysical Data Center (2010). *Santa Monica, California 1/3 arc-second NAVD 88 Coastal Digital Elevation Model*. NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, metadata gov.noaa.ngdc.mgg.dem:726 (published 2010-03-12). https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/metaview/page?xml=NOAA/NESDIS/NGDC/MGG/DEM/iso/xml/726.xml. Read through the NCEI ImageServer (`DEM_mosaics/DEM_all`, raster id 173) as a 216 x 270 px float32 export, `src/export_dem.py`

sources.S4: NOAA CO-OPS (2026). *Tidal datums, station 9410840 Santa Monica, CA* (34.0083 N, 118.5 W; 11.7 km from the site), epoch 1983-2001. https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/mdapi/prod/webapi/stations/9410840/datums.json?units=metric

caveats: Plan is the DESIGN layout (no as-built plan); crest level is a single sourced number (-6 ft MLLW at the apex); the top is assumed parallel to the seabed (state B), so the highest point is at the shoreward tips (-1.78 m MSL) and the V is shallower shoreward.
State A (top of bag -6 ft MSL = -1.829 m, level crest, Skelly drawing) is the alternative; both are the same number with two datum labels.
Reef is a V of geotextile sand bags ~1.2-1.35 m high (3.0 x 2.13 x 1.2 m bags); hence slopes are bag-stack flanks (1:1 assumed), not designed wave-transformation ramps.

The V arms are oblique to the model y axis and narrow (about 10-15 m), so any constant-x line crosses an arm over a few metres only: the crest-line ramp (1-2 m) is a tip artefact; the centreline crosses the apex block (ramp about 5 m). Use the stack height (1.35 m) and the 1:1 flank assumption instead of the line slopes.
Confidence in the 3D model is LOW (model.js confidence_3d).

centreline.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) at the alongshore mid-point of the reef footprint bounding box

crest_line.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) through the shallowest crest cell of the reef surface (ties within 0.02 m: the cell nearest the middle of the shallowest plateau)

second_crest_line.definition: cross-shore line through the shallowest reef cell on the OTHER side of the centreline than the main crest line (for two-arm reefs: the other arm); crest cell z = -1.87 m MSL

reconstruction_check.what: volume of the reef grid read here (sum of max(reef - seabed, 0) over all finite reef cells, no thickness threshold, seabed from this script) against the volume stated by the model for the same version; a check that the surface was reconstructed as the viewer draws it
